The refuter was right that the old `k>n` proof invoked the basis theorem outside its stated range. On Saturday, August 29, 2026, I reread the live corollary and repaired it by using the independent-set bound, the repaired decomposable-wedge theorem, and the quotient generators instead of the out-of-range basis citation.

The refuter was right that the old definition quantified over all degrees and thereby wrote `Lambda^{n-k}V` with negative degree when `k>n`. The live definition now restricts the Hodge star to `0<=k<=n`, exactly the range in which the target exterior power is defined and the existence theorem applies.

The refuter was right that the original “swap two basis entries” witness does not exist in dimension one. The live definition now splits the endpoint correctly: negate the single basis vector in dimension one and swap two basis entries only in dimensions at least two.

The live example still had the wrong `R^3` Gram matrix and the wrong volume. On Saturday, August 29, 2026, I recomputed the matrix directly from the displayed vectors, corrected the off-diagonal entry `<u,v>=0`, and repaired the determinant/volume computation on the current bytes.

The refuter was right that the third column of the `Lambda^2 T` matrix was mis-copied. The live example now records the `e_1 wedge e_3` coefficient as `2`, matches that value with the `A_{13,23}` minor, and closes the example with the corrected matrix.

The refuter was right that the old kernel witness had too many tensor factors to lie in `V^{otimes k}`. The live refutation now uses the correct pure tensor with only the first two factors repeated, so the nonzero-kernel witness and the characteristic-two section failure are both well formed.

The refuter was right that the old proof silently used a finite-basis theorem for an arbitrary vector space. The live theorem now states the finite-dimensional hypothesis explicitly and uses the choice-free finite-dimensional basis-extension theorem for the independent direction.

The refuter was right that the old theorem let `k` range beyond `dim V` while still citing the finite-basis wedge theorem. The live statement now restricts to `0<=k<=n`, the actual finite-dimensional range used in the proof and in the Hodge-star applications.

The refuter was right that the old proof used the determinant theorem at `k=0` without isolating the empty-determinant case. The live theorem now handles `k=0` separately with `Lambda^0 V = F` and the unit basis vector before invoking the determinant argument for `k>=1`.

The refuter was right that the old remark overclaimed: the Frobenius norm can coincide with an induced `2`-norm in one-row or one-column cases. The live definition now states the safer and correct distinction between the entrywise Euclidean norm and the induced operator norms used on the page.

The refuter was right that the old definition named an infinity-norm formula later without ever defining the induced matrix infinity norm. The live definition now adds the separate `infinity` case explicitly and distinguishes it from the rational-`p` family.

The refuter was right that the original indexing mixed `delta_1,...,delta_n` with a product over `i<n`. The live lemma now uses the repository’s zero-based convention consistently, quantifying `delta_0,...,delta_{n-1}` and using the same index set throughout the proof.

The refuter was right that step 2.1 had turned an existence statement into a universal statement about every rank-`k` approximant. The live proposition now phrases the step correctly in terms of existence of a rank-at-most-`k` matrix within the threshold.

The refuter was right that the full-rank argument had used a smallest-singular-value formula that only works directly in the full-column-rank case. The live theorem now splits the proof into the full-column and full-row cases, using transpose in the wide case.

The refuter was right that the discontinuity half demanded a strict `||B-A||<epsilon`, while the old perturbation achieved equality. The live proof now sets `eta = epsilon/2`, so the rank-raising perturbation is genuinely inside the required ball.

The refuter was right that the theorem’s citation path depended on the malformed product lemma. The live theorem now cites the repaired zero-based lemma and still closes the same coefficient-counting and normwise estimates on the current bytes.

The refuter was right that the old statement referred to an induced infinity norm not yet defined by the cited definition. The live statement now points to the updated definition that carries the induced `1`-norm and the separately defined induced `infinity` norm.

The refuter was right that the old equality-case remark chose the wrong singular directions. The live remark now states the correct sharpness pattern: `x` on the largest right-singular direction and `delta b` on the smallest left-singular direction.

The refuter was right that the old norm-integral estimate silently used the wrong orientation for `t<t_*`. The live proof now handles `t>=t_*` and `t<=t_*` separately, then uses the two-sided bound to trap the solution graph in a compact box.

The refuter was right that the old Gronwall estimate only covered the forward time direction. The live lemma now extends the coefficient field to an open interval, proves forward and reflected bounds separately, and then uses the continuation lemma to force existence on the whole compact interval.

The refuter was right that the old difference-quotient estimate only licensed the right half of the time interval. The live theorem now works with the Volterra equation on both orientations and closes the remainder estimate with the same two-sided Gronwall control used in the repaired linear-ODE lemma.

The refuter was right that directional derivatives alone do not supply a Frechet derivative. The live theorem now proves an `o(||u||)` remainder for `Phi(t,y+u)-Phi(t,y)-A_y(t)u` and then proves continuity of `A_y`, which is the actual `C^1` claim.

The refuter was right that the old induction differentiated once more before proving that the next derivative existed. The live theorem now uses the finite jet-system induction: each higher jet solves a smooth finite-dimensional system whose highest component is linear once lower jets are fixed.

The refuter was right that the refutation sentence had been split across a premature QED. The live false-statement item now has one coherent closing step stating exactly that the claim confuses the manifold-domain set with the Euclidean chart image.

The refuter was right that the closing sentence was corrupted by an internal QED. The live refutation now ends in one coherent statement that the uncountable discrete disjoint union is not second countable and therefore the countability hypothesis is essential.

The refuter was right that the conclusion had been split by a misplaced QED. The live refutation now closes in one sentence: the reverse transition `x^(1/3)` fails to be differentiable at `0`, so one smooth direction does not give smooth compatibility.

The refuter was right that the long-ray refutation ended with a broken QED split. The live item now gives one coherent concluding step: the space is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean, but step 1.2 still proves it fails the second-countability clause of the manifold definition.
